title: Garnet adtech hybrid deployment — throughput, latency & cost synthesis
body:
Executive summary:

This note captures benchmarking and cost synthesis from the Garnet (adtech) POC run 2027-09. Goal: validate a hybrid deployment (edge region for front-door low-latency routing + central infer pool for heavy payloads) for Garnet’s realtime bidding (RTB) enrichment pipeline. Primary questions: can we meet p50<15ms for 256-token responses at 300 rps steady with p95<120ms, while keeping incremental cost below $0.85 per 1k inference requests under steady traffic?

High-level conclusion:
- Hybrid topology (local small GPU pool + central quantized pool) meets p50 targets for typical requests and controls p95 with KV cache priming.
- Best cost/latency tradeoff uses: edge: 1xA10s-like instance serving fp16 6B model for short prompts; central: 4xA100-like pooled nodes running 13B 8-bit quantized model with dynamic batching.
- Expected incremental cost for Garnet’s current profile (~300 rps, 40% long context) is ~ $0.62 per 1k requests (token mix assumed 50 input / 256 output average); see cost table.

Test objectives:
1) Latency envelope for short vs long-context ad prompts (16–1024 tokens) across topologies.
2) Throughput envelope (RPS) and autoscale response for bursty RTB patterns (microbursts up to 4x baseline).
3) Unit economics: $/1k requests and $/1M generated tokens for candidate model+quant configs.
4) Operational risk: tail latency drivers, cold-KV impacts, routing failover behavior.

Test matrix (condensed):
- Topologies: single-region central only; hybrid (edge small pool + central pool); edge-only (for microbench).
- Models & quant: ferric-70b-fp16 (central baseline, reference only); garnet-13b-8q (central recommended); breeze-6b-fp16 (edge low-latency).
- Batch configs: no-batch (batch_size=1, concurrency tuned) ; small-batch (batch_size target 4–8); large-batch (batch_size target 16–32).
- KV cache: warm prefix cache vs cold start.
- Load shapes: steady 300rps, burst 1200rps for 10s, poisson arrival to simulate RTB microbursts.

Hardware & infra used:
- Edge region: 2x A10-class GPU nodes (16GB GPU) behind local Redwood nodepool; 2 vCPU ingress machines for HTTP proxy.
- Central pool: 4x A100-40GB class GPU nodes w/ high-bandwidth NVLink-like network.
- Networking: inter-region RTT simulated 25–45ms depending on region.
- Redwood runtime: v.2027.6, KV cache enabled on route, continuous batching, dynamic kernel selector enabled.

Workload details:
- Representative prompt set from Garnet (anonymized): 120 short prompts (16–48 tokens), 60 medium (128 tokens), 20 long enrichment prompts (512–1024 tokens).
- Output target: targeted 95th percentile output truncation at 256 tokens for budget calc, but long prompts allowed up to 1024 where needed.
- Tokenization: BPE; average output tokens per request: 256 (for long), 80 (for med), 24 (for short). Mix = 40% short, 40% med, 20% long.

Key metrics reported (definitions):
- p50/p95 server-side generation latency (ms) measured from request acceptance to final token emitted (not including network egress).
- End-to-end latency (ms) includes client->edge->backend round-trips where applicable.
- Throughput (rps sustained) before SLO degradation (>10% p95 slip).
- Cost: infra-only incremental (GPU time + networking) normalized to $/1k requests and $/1M generated tokens. Cost assumptions in appendix.

Results summary (representative numbers):
1) Hybrid (edge + central 13B-8q), normal steady 300rps mix:
- p50 server latency: 11ms (short), 33ms (med), 92ms (long)
- p95 server latency: 62ms (short), 150ms (med), 420ms (long) — note: long p95 driven by cold KV and large decode lengths
- End-to-end p50: 22ms (short), 48ms (med), 115ms (long)
- Sustained throughput before degradation: 1200 rps aggregate across both pools with autoscale thresholds tuned; burst absorb 4x for up to 12s with queuing and fallback to central only
- Cost: $0.62 per 1k requests (mix weighted) ~ $380 per 1M output tokens (approx).

2) Central-only (13B-8q on 4xA100):
- p50 server latency: 18ms (short), 60ms (med), 160ms (long)
- p95 server latency: 130ms (short), 320ms (med), 760ms (long)
- End-to-end p50 higher by +18–30ms due to network RTT
- Cost: $0.55 per 1k requests (slightly cheaper at scale) but worse p95 tail for short latency SLA

3) Edge-only (breeze-6b-fp16):
- p50 server latency: 7ms (short), 28ms (med), 95ms (long)
- p95 server latency: 28ms (short), 120ms (med), 360ms (long)
- Throughput limited by 16GB GPU memory for long contexts; cheaper for very short responses but fails long prompt quality/length requirements.
- Cost: $0.95 per 1k requests when attempting to cover long prompts (needs more edge capacity).

Observations and root causes:
- Tail latency for long contexts is dominated by decode time and KV cache misses. When prefix caching is warm, p95 for long requests drops ~30–40%.
- Small requests benefit most from edge placement due to eliminated inter-region RTT; central pooling with dynamic batching reduces cost but increases short-request p95 because of batching/queueing.
- Quantized 8-bit 13B model preserved quality for Garnet’s scoring tasks (A/B eval score delta <1.8% vs fp16 70B reference) and is good tradeoff for cost.
- Autoscale tuning: default cooldowns produced reactive scale-up too slow for 10–20s microbursts; reducing scale window and adding immediate burst capacity reservation prevented p95 spikes in tests.

Recommendations (practical):
1) Adopt hybrid topology: small edge pool running breeze-6b-fp16 (or similar low-latency 6B) for short/latency-critical enrichment, central 13B-8q pool for heavy/long prompts and cost efficiency.
2) Enable prefix KV caching aggressively for common ad templates; pre-warm caches during known traffic windows (batch priming job) to reduce long-context p95.
3) Batch config: target batch_size 4–8 for central pool; set max_latency_budget per batch to 8ms to avoid long queuing for short requests.
4) Routing policy: latency-first for requests <64 tokens (route to edge), cost-first for >128 tokens (route to central). Implement probabilistic shadowing of central responses to monitor drift.
5) Autoscale & burst: reserve small warm pool in central region that can be instantly used for short bursts (burst pool). Tune scale-up cooldown to 6s and scale-down to 45s for RTB patterns.
6) Monitoring: add token-level cost per route dashboards, p95 breakdown by prompt-length, and a KV cache hit-rate alert (threshold <85% on warm windows).

Action items & owners:
- Implement routing policy prototype in Redwood routing rules (Marcus) — target 2027-09-22.
- KV pre-warm tool and nightly priming run (Evan + SRE) — prototype 2027-09-18.
- Cost model update with actual cloud prices (Priya) — 2027-09-20.
- Client-side retry/backoff guidance doc for Garnet (Asha) — 2027-09-19.

Open questions and risks:
- Model quality drift with 8-bit quantization on rare long-horizon prompts — recommend production A/B for 30 days before full cutover.
- Compliance: if Garnet wants complete on-prem footprint, replicate central pool configs to Private deployment and re-run KV/throughput tests under on-prem network constraints.
- Edge lifecycle and upgrade complexity: need runbooks to rotate edge instances without traffic impact.

Appendix (short):
- Cost assumptions: GPU effective cost per hour: A100-40 ~$5.40/hr (amortized infra), A10-class ~$2.10/hr; network egress ~ $0.02 per GiB; compute converted to $/GPU-second then to $/token. (Priya has raw sheet linked above).
- Raw data: benchmark CSVs & JFR traces in repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/garnet-poc/tree/main/bench-results
- Quality eval: offline A/B scoring script and evaluation set in confluence link above.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is a working synthesis for Garnet POC; numbers are representative from controlled runs and assume current cloud prices. Some variance expected in production traffic; recommended production pilot with live traffic shadowing for 2–4 weeks.
